result.title: How do Transformers Perform Low-Level Control In-Context?
result.comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, Accepted to the 65th IEEE Conference on Decision and Control (CDC 2026)
result.summary: One of the remarkable abilities of Transformer-based neural networks is in-context learning. This motivates us to think about "in-context" control. Can we control a system knowing only (1) that it belongs to a particular family of systems and (2) some data on system evolution (provided as the context trajectory) but no specific parameter information? Specifically, we investigate the ability of Transformer-models to perform "in-context" control of unstable, nonlinear dynamical systems, where context consists only of the unforced system dynamics. We leverage a multi-head, GPT-2-style architecture, and we evaluate performance for two classical nonlinear systems -- the cartpole system and the two-link acrobot system, where the system parameters are unknown to the Transformer. We consider a setting where trajectories from an expert controller are available at training time but not at inference time. Here, we identify training techniques that are essential to train Transformers to perform low-level control. Through an analysis over checkpoints, we show that in-context control is possible, and the learned policy performance generally improves as context increases. Furthermore, the Transformer models can generalize to stabilize systems that are out-of-distribution.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 GPT-2 风格多头 Transformer 能否仅凭「系统族归属」与一段无控演化轨迹作为上下文，对参数未知的非线性系统（cartpole、acrobot）执行低层控制，并分析关键训练技巧、随上下文长度变化的性能以及分布外镇定能力。
AI.relevance_reason: 上下文轨迹实质是隐式系统辨识的证据，其随上下文增长而改善、并能外推到 OOD 的现象，可能为 LVR 中证据筛选、状态抽象与长度泛化的预测提供类比线索；但该工作无视觉或多模态成分，迁移价值尚待核查。
